newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ROOKIE DUNWOODY HELPS MARLINS SNARE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ROOKIE DUNWOODY HELPS MARLINS SNARE VICTORY.

text.p: Rookie Todd Dunwoody had three hits and drove in three runs Tuesday, including a game-winning single in the bottom of the ninth to lift the Florida Marlins to their eighth straight win, 6-5 over the New York Mets.

Dunwoody is batting .388 (7-for-18) with six RBI in seven games since winning play time after star right fielder Gary Sheffield suffered a sprained left thumb in last Tuesday's 11-5 win over the Atlanta Braves.
"I'm a young player and a rookie and I want to leave an impression," said Dunwoody, who turned 22 last month. "I will not sleep tonight, this is phenomenal. I'm walking on air."
Florida rallied for two runs in the last of the ninth after the Mets scored a pair in the top half to take a 5-4 lead.
Mets stopper John Franco (0-1), who had saves in his last nine appearances, was tagged with the loss.
Robb Nen (4-1) blew his third save but picked up the win despite allowing two unearned runs in the ninth.
In St Louis, Danny Jackson allowed one run and three hits over 6 1/3 innings in his season debut and and Ron Gant hit a solo homer as the Cardinals beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 3-1.

Jackson (1-0), who walked four and struck out five, had been sidelined since March 4, when he pulled muscles in his side in his first spring training start. He improved to 7-2 lifetime against his former team.
"It felt real good out there," Jackson said. "Physically I felt fine. I was nervous most of the night."
Pirates starter Esteban Loaiza (4-1) gave up two runs in seven innings as he fell to 0-5 lifetime against the Cards.
In San Francisco, Jeff Kent hit his third grand slam of the season and knocked in five runs to power the Giants to a 6-3 victory over the slumping Colorado Rockies.
Kent tied the franchise record for slams in a season when he connected on a 1-2 pitch from Roger Bailey in the first inning.
William VanLandingham (2-2) earned the win, going seven innings while giving up three runs. Bailey (4-4), who allowed six runs in seven innings, lost for the third straight time.
Ellis Burks and Vinny Castilla homered for Colorado, which has lost four straight and nine of its last 11 games.
In Atlanta, Terrell Wade allowed two runs over six innings and helped his cause with a tie-breaking RBI single as the Atlanta Braves beat the Montreal Expos 4-2.
Wade (2-3) gave up eight hits, walking one and striking out five for the victory. Mark Wohlers tossed a perfect ninth for his 10th save.
Fred McGriff had three hits for the Braves, while Wade keyed a two-run fourth inning by driving in a run with a two-out infield single.
Montreal starter Dustin Hermanson (1-3) took the loss.

In San Diego, Wally Joyner hit a three-run homer and Archi Cianfrocco drove in three runs to lead the Padres to a 7-3 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the first meeting between the teams since the last weekend of the 1996 regular season.
San Diego (17-25) swept three games from the Dodgers in the last weekend of 1996 to win the West Division title.
Sterling Hitchcock (4-4) earned the win, allowing one run and five hits over eight innings.
Ismael Valdes (2-5) yielded four runs and nine hits in six innings as the Dodgers lost for the fourth time in five games.
In Chicago, Mark Leiter allowed one run over eight innings and Ricky Bottalico pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the ninth as the Philadelphia Phillies edged the Cubs 3-2.
Leiter (4-4), won for the first time in five starts, allowing just three hits.
Bottalico allowed a run in the ninth and had the bases loaded with one out before striking out pinch-hitters Brooks Kieschnick and Mike Hubbard to notch his 11th save.
Rookie Scott Rolen hit a two-run homer in the first off starter Frank Castillo (2-6) and Gregg Jefferies added a solo shot in the seventh to account for the Philadelphia offence.
In Houston, Curtis Goodwin stroked four hits and Hal Morris had three hits and a pair of RBI as the Cincinnati Reds claimed a 7-4 victory over the Houston Astros.
With the score tied 3-3 and one out in the eighth inning, Morris doubled off reliever Russ Springer (1-2) and Willie Greene followed with a run-scoring single to give the Reds the lead for good.
John Smiley (4-6) allowed three runs and eight hits over seven innings for the win.
